# Generated by (transcript preserved so a reviewer can re-run it):
#
#   set versions {
#       0 1 1.0 1.0.0 1.2 1.2.0 1.2.3 1.3 1.10 1.2.10 2 2.0 2.3 10.0
#       1.2a1 1.2b1 1.3a1 1.3b1 1.3b2 1.2a2 0.9 9.0 8.6 8.6.14 9.0.4
#       1.0a1 1.0b1 2.0a1 1.2.3a1 1.2.3b4 3.1 3.0.1 0.0.1 100.200.300
#   }
#   set reqs {
#       1.2 1.2- 1.2-2.0 1.2-1.3 2 2- 0- 1.3b1 1.3b1- 1.2a1-1.3
#       1.0-2.0 1.2.3 9 8.5-9.0 1.10 1.2-1.2 2.0-2.0 1.2.0-1.2.0
#       1.3b1-1.3b1 0 1 10.0-  1.2.10 8.6-9.0 2.3-2.3 1.0.0-1.0.0
#   }
#   foreach a $versions { foreach b $versions {
#       puts "vcompare\t$a\t$b\t[package vcompare $a $b]" } }
#   foreach v $versions { foreach r $reqs {
#       puts "vsatisfies\t$v\t$r\t[package vsatisfies $v $r]" } }
#   foreach s {…} { puts "malformed-version\t$s\t[catch {package vsatisfies $s 1.2}]" }
#   foreach r {…} { set rc [catch {package vsatisfies 1.2 $r} res]
#       puts "malformed-req\t$r\t$rc\t[expr {$rc ? {} : $res}]" }
#
# Row formats (tab-separated):
#   vcompare          V1  V2   -1|0|1
#   vsatisfies        V   REQ  0|1
#   malformed-version V        1 (interpreter raised) | 0 (accepted)
#   malformed-req     REQ RC   RESULT-when-RC-is-0
#
# `malformed-*` rows pin the inputs the interpreter *rejects*: the port has no
# error channel, so it answers `false` where the interpreter raises, and the
# test asserts that mapping rather than a bare "does not panic".
